title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI hook with per-prompt thresholds and metrics integration
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Context: We need automated, per-prompt regression detection in our eval harness to prevent prompt-set quality regressions from landing. This PR introduces a CI hook that runs a lightweight eval against curated prompt sets and fails the job when configured per-prompt thresholds are exceeded. Motivation: Past incidents (see ENG-4321) showed regressions slipped through because aggregate metrics masked individual prompt failures. This CI hook surfaces per-prompt regressions and ties them to existing metrics dashboards for easier triage.

What this changes: added a new CI workflow (ci/workflows/eval-harness.yml) that runs the prompt-regression hook in PRs that touch model, prompt, or eval code; a Python CI hook (eval-harness/ci/prompt_regression_hook.py) that loads prompt sets, runs evaluations via the local eval runner, computes per-prompt metrics (accuracy, hallucination score, token-cost delta) and compares against thresholds in eval-harness/config/default_thresholds.json. When thresholds are exceeded the hook prints a summary and returns non-zero. Integrations: results are pushed to metrics/registry/prompt_metrics.yaml and a lightweight dashboard snapshot is written to observability/dashboards/prompt-regression.json. The hook supports a --dry-run mode used by maintainers and a --override-token to bypass gating for emergency fixes.

Testing and CI: added unit tests (tests/eval/test_prompt_regression.py) and integration smoke tests. The workflow retries flaky e2e evaluation once to reduce spurious failures. Local dev flow documented in eval-harness/docs/ci_integration.md. A small SDK helper was added (sdk/python/redwood_eval/__init__.py) to standardize the evaluation client used by the hook.

 rollout plan: merge to main, monitor the first 48h of CI runs, then enable the gating job for release/* branches. Owners: @Aisha Kumar (author), Priya Nair (on-call for CI), Michael Jensen (metrics/dashboards).

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke tests - [x] Metrics emitted to registry - [x] Docs updated - [x] Backwards compatible (default thresholds conservative)

References: ENG-4321, PM-987.

review_comments: Michael Jensen: Nice work — can we reduce false positives by applying a moving-average window for noisy prompts? Response: added conservative smoothing in the hook and documented behavior.

Priya Nair: Please confirm the CI image size and runtime. CI timings looked high on first run. Response: switched to a slim eval image and added a timeout for long-running prompts; runtime reduced ~40%.
Luca Romano: Need to make sure metrics names follow registry convention. Response: updated prompt_metrics.yaml to use 'eval.prompt.<metric>' and added unit tests asserting names.
Michael Jensen: Approve after CI green and tests updated. (approved)
Priya Nair: Approved — verified smoke tests locally. (approved)

release_notes: Adds a CI hook to detect per-prompt regressions in eval harnesses. Default thresholds are conservative; tooling publishes metrics to the prompt_metrics registry and writes a dashboard snapshot. Maintainers can run the hook in dry-run mode locally.
notes_for_ops: Monitor metric 'eval.prompt.regression_count' and CI failure rate for the first 48 hours post-merge. If noise appears, increase thresholds in eval-harness/config/default_thresholds.json or disable gating for specific prompt sets via .evalignore.
